texts.preamble: Bonthireddygari Narsimha Reddy vs The State Of Telangana on 14 August, 2024 Author: K. Lakshman Bench: K. Lakshman Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman Writ Petition No.22210 Of 2024 Oral Order
texts.facts: : This Writ Petition is filed under Article - 226 of the Constitution of India to declare the action of the respondents, more particularly respondent No.4 in binding over the petitioners under Section - 129 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS') on the request made by respondent No.5 and obtaining bond on 08.08.2024 for a period of one year without following due process of law, as illegal and arbitrary, and for consequential direction to the respondents not to interfere into the cultivation of the petitioners' lands. 3. According to the petitioners, there are disputes between the petitioners and their family members i.e., Bonthireddygari Sukendher Reddy and their sisters in respect of lands. They have also filed a suit vide O.S. No.304 of 2021 against them seeking KL,J perpetual injunction in respect of schedule - A and B properties mentioned therein which are situated at Isojipet Village, Pulkal Mandal,Sangareddy District. They have also filed an Interlocutory Application vide I.A. No.701 of 2021 seeking ad interim injunction, and vide order dated 27.07.2023, learned Junior Civil Judge-cum-Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Andole at Jogipet, granted ad interim injunction. i) Despite the same, since the defendants in the said suit being influential persons foisted several criminal cases against the petitioners. In the said process, respondent No.5 made a requisition to respondent No.4 to bind over the petitioners herein for keeping good behavior for a period of six (06) months stating that there are disputes in Survey Nos.76, 191, 192, 245, 289, 293, 175 and 302, situated at Isojipet Village of Pulkal Mandal and that such disputes may lead to disturbance to peace and tranquility of people in the Village and accordingly produced the petitioners before respondent No.4. In the said requisition, no details of crime etc., was mentioned by respondent No.5. KL,J Bonthireddygari Narsimha Reddy vs The State Of Telangana on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111900908/ 1 ii) On 08.08.2024, respondent No.4 bound over the petitioners under Section - 129 of the BNSS by way of accepting bonds for keeping good behavior for a period of one (01) year forcibly, or else to forfeit an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- without following any procedure laid down under law. On account of the said action of respondent Nos.4 and 5, the petitioners herein are unable to go and cultivate their lands, and thereby their livelihood is being affected. 4. Perusal of record would show that there are civil disputes pending between the petitioners and their other family members. A civil suit is also pending vide O.S. No.304 of 2021, wherein an ad interim injunction was also granted by learned Junior Civil Judge, Andole at Jogipet vide I.A. No.701 of 2021 on merits and the same is in subsistence.
texts.arguments: 5. However, it is contended by learned counsel for the petitioners that the police have no power to make a requisition under Section - 129 of the BNSS. In view of the said submission, it is apt to refer to Section - 129 of the BNSS, which is as under: "129. Security for good behaviour from habitual offenders. When an Executive Magistrate receives information that there is within his local jurisdiction a person who- (a) - - - - -, (b) - - - - -, or (c) - - - - -, or (d) - - - - -, or (e) habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of, offences, involving a breach of the peace, or (f) habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of- (i) any offence under one or more of the following. Acts, namely:- (a) - - - - -; (b) - - - - -; Bonthireddygari Narsimha Reddy vs The State Of Telangana on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111900908/ 2 (c) - - - - -; (d) - - - - -; (e) - - - - -; (f) - - - - -; (g) - - - - -; KL,J (ii) any offence punishable under any other law providing for the prevention of hoarding or profiteering or of adulteration of food or drugs or of corruption, or (g) is so desperate and dangerous as to render his being at large without security hazardous to the community, such Magistrate may, in the manner hereinafter provided, require such person to show cause why he should not be ordered to execute a bail bond, for his good behaviour for such period, not exceeding three years, as the Magistrate thinks fit." 7. It is apt to note that Section - 129 of the BNSS deals with 'security for good behaviour from habitual offenders', and the Executive Magistrate has to make an order under Section - 130 of the BNSS setting forth the substance of the information received, the amount of bond to be executed, the term for which it is to be in force and the number, character and class of sureties (if any) required. 8. As per Section - 173 (1) of the BNSS, every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, irrespective of the area where the offence is committed, may be given orally or by electronic communication to an officer in charge of a police station, and if given (i) orally, it shall be reduced to writing by him or under his direction, and be read over to the informant; and every such information, whether given in writing or reduced to writing as aforesaid, shall be signed by the person giving it; (ii) by electronic communication, it shall be taken on record by him on being signed within three days by the person giving it, and the substance thereof shall be entered in a book to be kept by such Officer in such form as the State Government may by rules prescribe in this behalf. In Banala Subhashini v. The State of Telangana 1, this Court had an occasion to deal with the scope and ambit of Section - 145 of the Code the powers of the Executive Magistrate, and by relying upon various judgments of Apex Court, it had held that the Executive Magistrate cannot pass any order, once there is anything to say that prima facie, any person in possession and once there is a civil matter pending. As per the said Section, when an Executive Magistrate receives information within his local jurisdiction, a person who, habitually commits, or attempts to commit, or abets the commission of offences, involving a breach of the peace, such Magistrate may, in the manner hereinafter provided, require such person to show cause why he should not be ordered to execute a bond, with sureties, for his good behaviour for such period, not exceeding three (03) years, as the Magistrate KL,J thinks fit.
